e.g. 2026-10-15T07:34:12.517Z. Screens show it in Pakistan time (UTC+5).
mfgDate and expDate on a certificate, e.g. Jun-2026.

{name or by, user, role} and often at: who did it, by login and role.

items.title: Glossary: words the team uses and what they mean in O2S

head: Word
Meaning in O2S
Where it comes from
rows: A customer's purchase order: 1 row in orders, with 1 or more lines.
1 product on 1 PO, with its own ordered, packed, dispatched and delivered Kg/L.
The bulk product the plant makes in batches (for example Sulfur Coated Urea). Many brands are packed from 1 base.
The product name on the bag the customer buys (for example Vital Urea, Naya S Urea).
1 production run of a base with its own batch number: a PO batch, a bulk batch or a multi-PO batch.
The output of 1 shift on a batch, numbered batch-L1, -L2. Each lot is tested on its own and gets its own COA.
1 packing entry: brand, Kg/L, packs, shift, in-charge and the batch number printed on the bag.
The batch number printed on the bag. The base batch number is the production batch it came from.
Certificate of analysis of a lot: drafted by a QC analyst (Lab Rep), reviewed by the AQCM, approved by the QCM. FIT or UNFIT.
The number on the COA, for example PQ0756.
A lot made and waiting for the lab.
The Plant Manager accepts an UNFIT lot with a written note; it goes on to the AQCM and the QCM.
An UNFIT lot sent by the Plant Manager back to Production with a reason; or off-spec material of the same base kept in a rework pool to be made again.
A packing run held after it failed its inspection; the Production Manager deals with it.
The QA check of a packed lot before it can go on a truck.
The QA check of a loaded truck. No truck is released without a pass. The report number is PSI- and the DC number.
An answer that counts as a pass; only on Price on the pack, with a reason.
The paper that goes with a truck: product, quantity and lot, never a price. Number = highest + 1.
The GP- paper that lets a truck or FOC sample out of the gate; issued after loading and a passed QA.
The transporter's bilty or other reference number for the truck. Optional.
All shipment rows with 1 dispId: 1 DC, 1 vehicle.
Truck planned, Loading, In transit, Delivered
Saad or Shoaib checks the truck after the gate pass, never Zain and never the one who made it. After 2 hours with no review the Plant Manager may release without it.
The Plant Manager's final approval; the DC is approved and dispatched counts.
The tap after the approved DC and gate pass are given to the driver. It closes the job, never holds the truck.
A refusal with a reason that lands on the Today of the person who must fix it.
Packed stock cleared by QA and not on a truck.
The customer collects with its own transport / VAN delivers.
Free of charge. An FOC sample (samples) is never an order; an FOC PO has every price at 0.
Over-production and extra material that FOC samples are taken from.
Key account manager: the sales person on a PO, and the reviewer of a new customer.
Supply Chain's check of whether the raw material for a line is in stock: full, partial or short.
Purchase request for raw material; the CFO approves it. Held on the line (rmPR) or, in the old model, in prs.
The receiving number typed when raw material arrives against a PR (receipts[].grn).
Supply Chain reads and accepts a new PO, or sends it back to whoever entered it.
The date promised for a line, from production rate, raw material and lead time.
Closing a line for less than ordered, with a reason; the Plant Manager approves; ordered never changes.
A cleared batch with no open order waiting. Not stuck; amber after 180 days so someone reviews it.
A batch with no output for 3 days, waiting for the lab 2 days, packed but open 2 days, or a line with nothing packed for 7 days while cleared stock is ready.
Any PO of the same client and product packed in the last 7 days; a moving line is not stuck.
A production run card for a bulk base when no batch of that base has logged output for 4 days.
Production's Today card, 1 per order line, when cleared base is ready for it.
The Pack from base card when the ready base is less than the line needs: X of Y ready.
The card when base already made and with the lab covers the rest.
Asks Production to make only what the ready base and the lab cannot cover.
Supply Chain's job on day 7 of a stuck line: close short, or waiting for client.
Supply Chain marks a line whose call-off has not come, with a reason and a date 1 to 30 days away. Not stuck until then.
A packing entry over 10,000 Kg/L, or 1 shift and in-charge over 10,000 Kg/L on 1 date. Saved, and the Production Manager marks it Seen.
The person who ran the line in that shift or packing run, picked from the In-charge list; never the person typing.
The quantity unit: Kg for a solid product, L for a liquid.
Number of bags or bottles: Kg/L divided by the pack size.
Accounting for a batch's unpacked remainder: loss, by-product, diverted, rework, or kept as bulk stock. It does not close the batch.
Material from a batch routed to another base (Sulfur Coated Urea to Nitro Sulfur), held in a by-product pool and later called up as its own batch.
QC-cleared material of the same product put in a divert pool at reconcile; packed or recycled later with no new QC.
An open batch with no batch number holding by-product, diverted or rework material for 1 base.
Kg/L lost at reconcile, with a reason / the remainder written off by reconcile.
Ending production on a batch, with the yield and, when short, the reason. The Plant Manager is told.
1 batch made for several PO lines at once.
Imported stock rows from before go-live; removed by the June purges (COO: no opening balances).
Moving packed stock to another PO of the same customer and product; the bags stay, the record moves.
The screen for fixing a wrong entry with a reason, in your name; each fix goes in the corrections register.
Ways a record is ended without being removed (DD-10).
An entry keyed after its allowance; it needs a reason and counts against the department.
The list of jobs waiting on the signed-in role.
Putting a Today job off until a date with a reason.
A job more than 1 person can do; when 1 of them does it, it closes for both. Taking it (opening it from Today) only shows 'X is on it' to the others for 8 hours; it does not lock or close the job.
The area for master data, users, departments and checks (COO, CFO, Plant Manager).
A lab person named by the Plant Manager to sign 1 line for the AQCM or QCM on leave.
The sales tax on orders. On an FED-inclusive price the net is price / 1.05.
Counted the day the truck leaves the gate: quantity x invoice price, net of FED.
The price printed on the bag: the PO's own price, or the list price, or none.
The sales order number in the ERP; required on every PO; prints on the DC.
Products made for another company's brand (for example LCI, Maxim, Syngenta).
The channel for VITAL AGRI NUTRIENTS (PVT) LTD's own orders.
The VGreen channel and its 2 outlets: Value Chain and Farm Management.
A one-time page of what changed; each part answered, then signed by typing your name.
From 16b: the month and year of the packing date, not the production date.

1 product and 1 batch number on the bag packed in 2 or more months, on any PO, with at least 1 run packed from 16b (older runs count with their printed month); the Production Manager confirms it with a note.
On the QA sheets: the close date of the batch the run was packed from, for information. An open batch shows Batch not closed yet; a divert pool shows nothing.
Picker under the packing run table in Batch trace: pick a 16b run and correct the Mfg month on the bag and the month printed on the bags, nothing else (Production, COO).

src: Guide rule Alerts on your phone and laptop

head: Word
Meaning in O2S
Where it comes from
rows: A message on the phone or laptop, also with O2S closed, when a Today job reaches you.
1 browser on 1 phone or laptop where a person switched alerts on.
The button on the Today card that switches this device on.
The browser refuses alerts for O2S; allow them in the site settings.
The list of all Today jobs an open screen sends, for clock jobs and escalations.
1 alert per person with the jobs held from 10 pm.
On iPhone, O2S added from Safari as an icon; alerts work only from there.

items.title: Complaints: the words (16e)

head: Word
Meaning in O2S
Where it comes from
rows: A customer’s report of a fault in a delivered product, kept in O2S with its own number.
Holding and checking the same batch still at VAN, within 24 hours; calling other customers who got it.
A packing run held by a complaint: not free, cannot be loaded, passed out or released.
Asking why up to 5 times, each answer with its evidence, until the cause is something VAN can act on.
A line of whys: why it happened; why our check did not catch it; a second cause.
What is done for this case now.
What removes this root cause; it has a test that shows the fix worked.
What stops the same on other products or lines.
The 1 department, person or outside party mainly responsible.
The facts cannot be found; Tahir accepts it with his name.
The paper for the customer: what was found and done, in Tahir’s words.
Tahir marked away: the Plant Manager does his complaint jobs.
Monday to Saturday, not a holiday on the list.
Packed stock that cannot be inspected or shipped until its hold is lifted: on complaint hold or QA hold. Shown under its own heading with why.
An order whose packed stock is all on complaint hold; its next step is the complaint.
A truck that left the gate and returned; when approved, its release is undone and its DC and gate pass are cancelled.

The reason the Production Manager writes on a cleared batch that is not being packed.
The batch is being processed and will be ready in 1 week; not stuck for 7 days.
Kept for another client whose PO is expected by a date (1 to 30 days); still offered for packing.
Plant, Stuck batches: the cleared batches with a reason standing.
